item.text:
**4B.8: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi in 2024**

Overall judgment: **No, not in a substantive sense.**  
He did complete a formal constitutional inauguration for a new term, but the 2024 record shows continuity of an already entrenched third term, no meaningful succession opening, and continued reliance on loyal insiders rather than a real transfer or coalition-based handoff.

**Accepted claims**
- **Formal oath-taking before parliament for a new six-year term** | State Information Service | 2024-04-02 | [URL](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-el-sisi-takes-the-constitutional-oath-for-new-presidential-term/) | Sisi was sworn in before the House of Representatives under Article 144, which is procedural evidence of a constitutional inauguration. This supports only a narrow, formal-positive reading of transfer-of-power compliance. | QIDs: 4B.8
- **Presidency framed the oath as constitutional continuity, not a handoff to a successor** | Presidency of the Republic of Egypt | 2024-04-02 | [URL](https://www.presidency.eg/en/%D9%82%D8%B3%D9%85_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9/event242024/) | The presidency described the event as the start of a new presidential term and repeated Sisi’s pledge to uphold the constitution. This shows formal procedure, but not respect for succession rules or term-limit restraint. | QIDs: 4B.8
- **Freedom House says Sisi secured a third term in a noncompetitive election after term-length changes** | Freedom House | 2024 | [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House states that 2019 amendments extended Sisi’s current term through 2024 and that he then secured a third six-year term in an election with arrests and intimidation. That is strong evidence against genuine respect for term limits. | QIDs: 4B.8, 4B.1, 4B.2
- **HRW says authorities jailed and banned Tantawy for challenging Sisi** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-06-04 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/04/egypt-opposition-leader-imprisoned) | HRW says Ahmed Tantawy and supporters were imprisoned and barred from future elections after a peaceful challenge to Sisi. This cuts against any claim that succession or transfer rules were meaningfully open to contestation. | QIDs: 4B.8, 4B.1, 4B.2, 4B.5
- **Reuters reported Sisi moved defense leaders into presidential adviser roles in a July reshuffle** | Reuters via Yahoo | 2024-07-03 | [URL](https://www.yahoo.com/news/egypts-sisi-names-ex-defence-140545714.html) | The defense minister and chief of staff were replaced, but both outgoing officials were retained as presidential advisers. That suggests managed elite rotation inside the same security network, not a real succession transition. | QIDs: 4B.8, 4B.5
- **Reuters reported the intelligence chief was replaced by his deputy and then kept close as an adviser** | Reuters via MarketScreener | 2024-10-16 | [URL](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Egypt-s-Sisi-replaces-head-of-powerful-general-intelligence-agency-48090165/) | The outgoing intelligence chief became an adviser to the presidency, and Reuters noted the agency’s domestic-security role under Sisi. This looks like continuity and consolidation, not preparation for institutionalized succession. | QIDs: 4B.8, 4B.5
- **Sisi’s July cabinet message emphasized institutional coordination, not transfer of power** | State Information Service | 2024-07-03 | [URL](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-el-sisi-meets-prime-minister-and-members-of-the-new-government/) | Sisi told the new government to strengthen institutional frameworks, coordination, integrity, and transparency. That is a governance signal, but it does not evidence any real acceptance of succession limits or coalition transfer. | QIDs: 4B.8, 4B.4

**Search gap**
- I found **no credible 2024 evidence** of Sisi voluntarily preparing a handoff to a successor, honoring a meaningful coalition constraint, or accepting a genuine constitutional transfer of power beyond the formal swearing-in ceremony.
- The positive evidence is procedural only: a constitutional oath, parliamentary ceremony, and cabinet reshuffle. The substantive record is continued incumbency, opposition suppression, and elite recycling within the same security state.
